Date 8th January 1941

REPORT

Subject ANNUAL PARADE OF THE JAPANESE NAVAL LANDING PARTY.

Made by and Forwarded by Inspector J. Watson
Officer i/c.

Sir,

I have to report that at 10 a.m. 7-1-41. the annual
parade, and review of the Japanese Naval Landing Party,
was held at Hongkew Park. Mechanised units were inspected
on Kiangwan Road. Following the inspection "Mechanised
Units" proceeded south on North Szechuen Road, Japanese
Naval Landing Party Units on foot headed by the Naval
Band, and buglers proceeded along Luxwell Road, whilst
another detachment marched south on North Szechuen
Road. Many high ranking Japanese Naval, and Military
Officials attended, as well as representatives of
America, Great Britain, France, and Italy.

Extra Police were posted at all important points
in the vicinity of Hongkew Park, North Szechuen Road,
and Luxwell Road. A large number of Japanese civilians,
and school children visited Hongkew Park. The crowd
was estimated to number about 10,000.

No untoward incident reported.

Traffic was held up for a short period during the
parade.

主题：日本海军陆战队年度阅兵。

由督察 J. Watson 撰写并呈报
主管警官

先生，

谨此报告，1941年1月7日上午10时，日本海军陆战队的年度阅兵及校阅在虹口公园举行。机械化部队在江湾路接受了检阅。检阅结束后，“机械化部队”沿北四川路向南行进，日本海军陆战队步兵分队由海军军乐队和号手引领，沿禄思威尔路行进，另一分队则沿北四川路向南行进。许多日本海军和军方高级官员出席，美国、英国、法国和意大利的代表也出席了活动。

在虹口公园、北四川路和禄思威尔路附近的所有重要地点均部署了额外警力。大量日本平民和学生参观了虹口公园。估计人群数量约为10,000人。

未报告发生任何意外事件。

阅兵期间交通短暂受阻。

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

GRAND NAVAL REVIEW TO BE HELD HERE ON JANUARY 7

Admiral Shimada, Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese China Seas Fleet, will inspect and Rear Admiral Takeda, Commander of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, will command the grand naval review to be held in the vicinity of Kiangwan Road and Hongkew Park from 10 a.m. January 7 according to the following programme :-
1) March past of mobile units in front of the Shanghai Jinja Shrine.
2) Review of rifle-units on Hongkew Park.
3) March past of rifle-units in Hongkew Park.
4) Review of dogs and carrier-pigeons in the military service in Hongkew Park.
5) Review of formations of carrier-pigeons at Hongkew Park.
After the above-mentioned review, processions with naval ensigns in the lead will be carried out over the following routes :-
1) The main-gate of Hongkew Park-Kiangwan Road-North Szechuen Road-Paoshing Road-Paoshan Road.
2) The main-gate of Hongkew Park-North Szechuen Road-Dixwell Road-Urga Road-Sinkeipang Road-Seward Road.
3) The back-gate of Hongkew Park-Kiangwan Road-North Szechuen Road-Tientungan Road-Paoshing Road-Chungsan Road.
4) The back-gate of Hongkew Park-Kiangwan Road-West Recreation Road-Urga Road-Ziang Wei Road-Scott Road-North Szechuen Road-Tung Chi Road.
5) The main-gate of Hongkew Park-North Szechuen Road-North Soochow Road.
6) The main-gate of Hongkew Park-Kiangwan Road-North Szechuen Road-Dixwell Road-Kashing Road-Woosung Road.
In case of inclement weather, the review will be postponed until January 8 and in that case, a notice will be issued.

《大陆新报》

1月7日将在本地举行大型海军校阅

日本中国方面舰队司令长官岛田繁太郎海军中将将进行检阅，日本海军陆战队司令武田盛治海军少将将指挥于1月7日上午10时在江湾路及虹口公园附近举行的大型海军校阅，程序如下：
1) 机动部队在上海神社前分列式行进。
2) 在虹口公园检阅步枪部队。
3) 步枪部队在虹口公园分列式行进。
4) 在虹口公园检阅军用犬和信鸽。
5) 在虹口公园检阅信鸽编队。
上述校阅结束后，将以海军旗为前导，按以下路线进行游行：
1) 虹口公园正门-江湾路-北四川路-宝兴路-宝山路。
2) 虹口公园正门-北四川路-狄思威路-乌尔嘎路-新记浜路-西华德路。
3) 虹口公园后门-江湾路-北四川路-天潼路-宝兴路-中山路。
4) 虹口公园后门-江湾路-西娱乐场路-乌尔嘎路-祥伟路-斯科特路-北四川路-同济路。
5) 虹口公园正门-北四川路-北苏州路。
6) 虹口公园正门-江湾路-北四川路-狄思威路-嘉善路-吴淞路。
如遇恶劣天气，校阅将推迟至1月8日，届时将发布公告。

Subject Parade by the Japanese Naval Landing Party at the New Year.
Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

The Japanese Naval Landing Party in Shanghai
will hold a parade in celebration of New Year under
the command of Rear-Admiral Takeda, Commander of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party, The parade will take
place on Kiangwan Road and in Hongkew Park commencing
at 10 a.m. January 7th, 1941, and Admiral Shimada,
Commander-in-Chief of the Japanese Fleet in China
waters, will inspect the units.
Mechanized units comprising 83 vehicles
including tanks, armoured-cars, motor-trucks, motor-cars,
and motorcycles, will assemble on Kiangwan Road North
of the West Gate of Hongkew Park before 10 a.m. on
January 7th and will proceed South along Kiangwan Road
and pass in review at 10 a.m.. The salute will
be taken by Admiral Shimada in front of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party barracks on Kiangwan Road.
Following the salute the marching units will march
by way of North Szechuen, Boone, Woosung, Kashing,
Dixwell, North Szechuen Roads and thence to the Naval
Landing Party Barracks.
Infantry units will assemble inside Hongkew
Park prior to 10 a.m. and following the reviewing of
the mechanized units, Admiral Shimada will proceed to
the park, where a march past of infantry units will
take place.
The proceedings are expected to last about one
hour. After the parade, one infantry unit will

Admiral Oikawa will proceed to Hongkew Park, where he
will review the parade of other units. The whole

a half.

JAN 4 1940

Naval Landing Party
To be Reviewed

Parade to Be Held Next
Sunday in Hongkew Park

Admiral Koshiro Oikawa, com-
mander-in-chief of the Japanese
China Seas Fleet, will review
Japanese naval forces in Shanghai on
Sunday in a revival of the annual
New Year parade, it was officially
announced yesterday.

Rear-Admiral Moriharu Takeda,
commandant of the Japanese Special
Naval Landing Party in Shanghai,
will be in command of the marching
forces.

The review of mechanized forces
will start at 11 o'clock on Sunday
morning on Kiangwan Road near
Hongkew Park. It will be followed
by a review and a march past of the
forces on foot in the park, the an-
nouncement stated.

The participating units will return
to their quarters by marching
through Hongkew streets, according
to the announcement.

Last year the parade was not held.

Sir,

approximately 200 officers and men of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party, operated in the portion of this district bounded by
Glen, Yangtsepoo, Kweiyang and Hochien Road.

Sir,
I beg to report that between 8 a.m. - 11 a.m. on 9-6-37,
approximately 200 officers and men of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party held manoeuvres in the portion of this district
bounded by Linching, Kweiyang, Hochien and Yangtszepoo Roads.
This force was divided into two parties and each party
into an attacking and defending force. One of the parties
carried out tactical exercises west of Glen Road whilst the
other, which was assisted by one large and one small tank,
armoured cars and motor cycles carried out similar operations
east of Glen Road.
Blank rifle and machine gun ammunition was fired.
The large tank when turning at the intersection of Glen
and Pingliang Roads damaged the soft road surface.
